Welcome to KeyAble.

KeyAble allows you to customize your Keychron keyboard and is fully accessible for screen reader users with an easy-to-use interface. It supports various Keychron keyboards and has been tested on the Q6 Max, V5 Max, V6 Max, and B6 Pro.

KeyAble is an independent app and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Keychron. We have tested it as thoroughly as we can, but we cannot test every model, layout and computer, so please treat it as use-at-your-own-risk software.

The good news is that remapping does no lasting harm: you can reset any key, or the whole keyboard, from within the app. You can also reset the keyboard to its factory settings without the app, using a key combination on the keyboard itself; see Help for more details.

    Step 1. Connect Your Keyboard to KeyAble.

    ○ Keyboard Not Connected to KeyAble. Please follow instructions below to connect.

    In order to make changes to your keyboard you need to connect it to the KeyAble software. Make sure your keyboard is connected to your computer with a USB cable and that the connection type switch is set to USB cable mode and not Bluetooth or 2.4GHz wireless. Not all browsers support USB connectivity. KeyAble has been tested on Edge, Chrome, and Brave.

    You have previously used your current keyboard with KeyAble. Would you like to connect it again?

    Keyboard Not Supported.

    KeyAble does not recognise this device. To remap keys safely, KeyAble needs to know your keyboard's exact layout. Without it, writing to the wrong key position could silently remap a different key.

    If your keyboard is on Bluetooth or 2.4 GHz, the device you chose may be the wireless receiver rather than the keyboard. Set the connection switch on the keyboard to cable, plug in the USB cable, choose Disconnect and Go Back, and connect again.

    Method 2. Use Capture Mode To Select Key.

    Capture mode asks your keyboard which key you pressed. Press the Start Capture Mode button, then press the key you want to select for customisation. Your selection is confirmed automatically and capture mode ends. To cancel without selecting a key, press Escape twice quickly or press the Stop Capture Mode button.

    The keyboard reports where the key is, not what it types, so a key is found even if it has been remapped or set to do nothing, and even if your screen reader uses it. Press one key at a time: two keys together, such as Control and C, select neither. For a knob, turn it or press it. Pressing the knob also mutes your sound as usual, so press it again afterwards to unmute.

    Windows key note: Pressing the Windows key during capture will open the Start menu - this is an operating system restriction that cannot be prevented. The key will still be captured. Simply close the Start menu and return to this page to continue.

    Press the key you want to select. Capture will end automatically and confirm your selection. Press Escape twice quickly or press Stop Capture Mode to cancel.

    You have selected:

    When ticked, your new action only happens while you hold Fn and press this key, for example Fn plus Home. The key keeps its normal action when Fn is not held. Leave this unticked to change what the key does on its own.

      Help.

      Welcome to the help section. KeyAble lets you customize your Keychron keyboard: remap any key, build macros, control the backlight, and back up your setup, all using your keyboard and screen reader alone. This guide covers how to get started, what is new in this version, which keyboards are supported, what KeyAble cannot do yet, the emergency reset shortcut if anything ever goes wrong, and answers to the questions we are asked most often. In KeyAble, Alt plus a number, 1 through 6, returns you to any step at any time.

      Getting Started in Three Steps.

      Changing a key takes three steps, one for each of the first three sections of KeyAble.

      1. Go to Step 1, Connect, and connect your keyboard with a USB cable. After the first time, a quick reconnect button appears so you do not need the browser dialog again.
      2. Go to Step 2, Choose a Key, and pick the key you want to change, either from the list or by pressing it in Capture Mode.
      3. Go to Step 3, Choose an Action, and pick what that key should do from the tabs: a single key, a keyboard shortcut, a media control, a system key, a macro, or nothing at all. A Ready to Apply dialog then reads back the change; choose Apply Remap to write it to the keyboard, or Change Action or Change Key to go back.

      Your changes are saved straight onto the keyboard, so they stay with it even on another computer.

      What's New.

      Version 1.5, 19th November 2026

      • 60 more models, including the wired Q and V series, the K Pro and Q Pro ranges, the K17 Max and more Max models, and the C1, C2 and C3 Pro.
      • A model not yet tested on a real keyboard says so when it connects, with a Tell Us How It Went button that starts an email with your keyboard's details filled in.
      • A new macro no longer takes a slot that one of Keychron's macro keys (M1 to M5) plays, so those keys keep their macros.
      • The Menu, Sleep and Keychron macro keys are now named when you choose a key.

      Version 1.4, 17th November 2026

      • Backups now save the whole keyboard: every key on every layer, the knob, macros, lighting and Keychron's own settings. Restoring changes only what differs from the backup. Backups made by version 1.3 or earlier cannot be restored.
      • Nine HE (Hall Effect) models: the Q1, Q3, Q5, Q6, K2, K4, K6, K8 and K10 HE. Their actuation point and rapid trigger still need Keychron's Launcher.
      • The B1 Pro, and the B6 Pro in its US layout. Both work in their original and 2025 versions.
      • RGB Lighting saves each setting before changing the next, so the keyboard keeps all of them.
      • Reset Keyboard to Default Settings no longer reports success when the keyboard refuses the reset.

      Version 1.3, 10th November 2026

      • Three new models: the K3 Max, K5 Max and S1.
      • 17 Ultra 8K models, built from Keychron's firmware source. None has been tested on a real keyboard yet, so reports are very welcome. Supported Keyboards lists them.
      • A new System Key for Windows: Voice Typing (Win+H).
      • The B6 Pro has its full UK layout, including F13, Calculator, Task View and the two desktop keys. Its factory settings now come from Keychron's own firmware, so Review Changes and resets are right on its Fn layer too.
      • Capture Mode finds the key you press by where it is on the keyboard, not by what it types. It now works on keys you have remapped, keys set to do nothing, and keys your screen reader uses.
      • Mission Control and Launchpad now work on the wired Q and V keyboards and on the K2 Pro and K6 Pro. Macros and RGB lighting now work on the K2 Pro and K6 Pro.
      • Resetting a key restores what Keychron's released firmware actually ships. On many keyboards this differed from Keychron's published source code.
      • Corrected key layouts for the Q1, Q1 Max, Q6, K2 Pro and K6 Pro, and for the V6 Max ANSI's Right Shift and Numpad 0. The K2 Pro and K6 Pro gain their lighting key.
      • Reading your keyboard is faster: a whole layer is read at once instead of key by key. Reads can no longer get mixed up, which could put the wrong keys in a backup or in Review Changes.
      • A backup made on a layout that has since changed is refused rather than restored onto the wrong keys. Restoring a backup from version 1.2 onto a V6 Max ANSI leaves Right Shift and Numpad 0 as they are, and tells you to make a new backup.
      • Turning RGB lighting off now stays off. Going back to RGB Lighting no longer shows it as on.
      • Each connection starts on the layout your keyboard's Mac or Windows switch is set to, instead of the last one you chose.
      • Demo mode simulates the model you choose, with its real factory settings, so every feature can be tried without a keyboard.
      • The key after Print Screen on the V3, V6 and Q6 is now called Voice Assistant.

      We have tested the B6 Pro ISO, Q6 Max ISO, V5 Max ISO and V6 Max ISO on real hardware. The rest are built from Keychron's own firmware data and should work. When one connects, Step 1 shows a Tell Us How It Went button: please use it, whether it works or not. If your keyboard connects but is not recognised, Step 1 shows a keyboard ID and a Report This Keyboard ID button so we can add it.

      On the HE (Hall Effect) models, KeyAble does everything it does on other keyboards, and sets their actuation point in Keyboard Settings. Rapid trigger and their other settings still need Keychron's Launcher.

      Not supported: the HE and Ultra 8K models not listed here, such as the Q0 HE, the HE 8K models and the V2 Ultra 8K. See "Does KeyAble work with HE or Ultra 8K keyboards?" in Frequently Asked Questions.

      What KeyAble Can't Do Yet.

      Keychron's own Launcher app can do a few things that KeyAble cannot do yet:

      • Change keys on layers other than the Mac or Windows layer and its Fn layer, for example the Fn2 layer.
      • Assign keys that switch between layers.
      • Keys that hold several modifiers at once, such as Hyper (Ctrl, Shift, Alt and Windows) and Meh (Ctrl, Shift and Alt). A single key can already send all four modifiers with another key, from Build a Keyboard Shortcut.
      • Mouse keys, which move the pointer or click from the keyboard.
      • Keys that change the backlight when pressed. The backlight itself is fully controllable from the RGB Lighting section.
      • Keychron's Bluetooth, 2.4 GHz and battery check keys.
      • Japanese and Korean input keys, and Japanese (JIS) keyboard layouts.
      • Keyboard-wide settings other than debounce, the wireless sleep times and the Ultra 8K keyboards' polling rate, such as the polling rate of other keyboards.
      • Settings of HE (Hall Effect) keyboards other than one actuation point for every key, such as rapid trigger and an actuation point for each key.
      • The HE and Ultra 8K keyboards not in Supported Keyboards, such as the Q0 HE, the HE 8K models and the V2 Ultra 8K.

      The audio and music mode keys are left out on purpose: they need a speaker in the keyboard, which Keychron keyboards don't have. Firmware updates are left out too: a failed update can leave a keyboard unusable, so use Keychron's Launcher for these.

      Emergency Reset. No App Required.

      If your keyboard ever gets into an unexpected state, you can restore all keys to their factory defaults directly from the keyboard without needing this app or a computer. Hold Fn + J + Z for 4 seconds. On a keyboard with two Fn keys, if one does not work, try the other.

      The backlight flashes briefly to confirm the reset. To check without seeing it, press a key you had remapped: it does its normal job again. Or, in this app, Review Changes on This Keyboard lists no changed keys.

      Frequently Asked Questions.

      Answers to the questions we are asked most often, from browsers and cables to macros, sounds, and what to do if something goes wrong.

      Which keyboards does KeyAble work with?

      Keychron keyboards in ANSI and ISO layouts; Japanese JIS layouts are not supported yet. Supported Keyboards has the full list of models, and says which we have tested on real hardware; the others are built from Keychron's firmware data and should work.

      Does KeyAble work with HE or Ultra 8K keyboards?

      Most of them, yes. The Ultra 8K models run ZMK firmware rather than QMK, but Keychron's ZMK includes the same VIA connection KeyAble uses, so they connect like any other model. Supported Keyboards lists them. None has been tested on a real keyboard yet, so please tell us how yours goes. A few are not supported yet, such as the V2 Ultra 8K, which has two Fn layers for each system.

      The HE (Hall Effect) models in Supported Keyboards work like any other: remapping, macros, lighting and backups. They are built from Keychron's released firmware, like most models. Their magnetic switches also have settings of their own. KeyAble sets one actuation point for every key, in Keyboard Settings; rapid trigger, an actuation point for each key and the other HE settings still need Keychron's Launcher. Some HE models are not supported yet, such as the Q0 HE and the HE 8K models. Keyboards KeyAble does not support can be set up with Keychron's own Launcher.

      Which web browser do I need?

      Use a Chromium-based browser such as Chrome, Microsoft Edge, or Brave. These browsers can talk to your keyboard directly over USB. Firefox and Safari cannot do this yet, so KeyAble will not be able to connect in them.

      Can I try KeyAble without a keyboard?

      Yes. In Step 1, choose Try KeyAble Without a Keyboard (Demo), then pick any model from the list. KeyAble then works with a pretend keyboard of that model, starting at its factory settings, so every step behaves as it would with the real one: remapping, macros, lighting, Review Changes, backup and reset. Nothing is written to a keyboard, and the pretend keyboard is forgotten when you disconnect or close KeyAble.

      Do I have to keep the USB cable plugged in?

      Yes, but only while you are making changes. Remapping needs the wired USB connection. Once your changes are saved you can unplug the cable and go back to Bluetooth or wireless. Your changes stay on the keyboard.

      Will my changes still work on another computer?

      Yes. Everything you set up is saved into the keyboard's own memory, not onto this computer. Plug the keyboard into any machine and your keys, macros, and lighting behave the same, as long as the OS slide switch on the back is set to the same side you made the change for. See the next question if you switch between Mac and Windows.

      I use this keyboard on both a Mac and a Windows PC. What should I pick?

      The keyboard stores a separate Mac layout and Windows layout, chosen by the slide switch on the back. Step 3 says which layout your changes go to, and KeyAble picks the one that matches the switch. If it cannot read the switch, it asks you to choose before your first change. To change it, use the "Choose Mac or Windows Layout" button. Your choice lasts until the keyboard disconnects: each new connection starts on the layout that matches the switch. If you move the one keyboard between a Mac and a Windows computer and want a change on both, make it once for each layout: shortcuts and System Keys use different keys on a Mac and on Windows. If a change seems to disappear, check that the slide switch matches the layout you edited.

      Do I need to install anything? Is it safe?

      No installation and no internet. KeyAble runs entirely in your browser and talks only to the keyboard in front of you. It has no accounts, and collects or sends no data about you, your keyboard, or how you use it.

      It is a single self-contained file with no third-party code fetched from the web. It reaches your keyboard through the browser's WebHID feature, and only after you pick your keyboard from the browser's permission prompt; you can withdraw that permission at any time. Text you type into a macro, and anything your keyboard reports back, is only ever shown as plain text, never run as code, so a faulty keyboard cannot make the app do anything unintended.

      I pressed Connect but my keyboard is not in the list. What now?

      Check two things. One, the cable is a full USB data cable, not a charge-only cable. Two, the switch on the keyboard is set to cable or wired mode, not Bluetooth or 2.4 GHz. Then press Connect again. It can take a moment for the keyboard to appear, so keep checking the Connect button in the browser dialog.

      The list can also show the 2.4 GHz wireless receiver, often named Keychron Link. That is not your keyboard, and KeyAble cannot use it. Set the switch to cable and choose the keyboard by its own name instead.

      What is VIA, and do I need to turn it on?

      VIA is the system KeyAble uses to read and change your keyboard's keys over USB. Keychron's QMK keyboards have it built in and always on, so there is nothing to turn on. If your keyboard connects but does not respond, check the switch is set to cable. Very old firmware may not include VIA; updating it with Keychron's own Launcher fixes that.

      Can I undo a change?

      Yes, in several ways. In Step 2, Reset This Key To Default Action puts a single key back, including its Fn action. In Step 1, Review Changes on This Keyboard lists every key you have changed on the current layout and lets you reset any of them, and Reset Keyboard to Default Settings resets everything. Before making big changes you can also save your setup to a file from Step 1, then restore it later if you change your mind.

      What does a saved setup hold?

      Every key on every layer, the knob, your macros and the lighting. On keyboards whose firmware has them, it also holds Keychron's own settings, such as debounce and the wireless sleep times, and Keychron's own lighting, such as per-key colours. A file restores onto the same keyboard model only, and only what differs is written.

      If the keyboard's firmware has been updated since the file was saved, keys set to Keychron's own functions and the lighting effect are left as they are, because their numbers can change between firmware versions. Before you confirm, KeyAble says what will be left alone, and it says so again when the restore finishes.

      Setups saved by KeyAble 1.3 or earlier cannot be restored by this version.

      Does Reset Keyboard to Default Settings delete my macros too?

      Yes. It returns every key on every layer to its factory setting and clears all macro slots. If you want to keep your macros, save your setup to a file first.

      Why was I warned that a key is risky to remap?

      A few keys are important for keeping control of your keyboard and your screen reader, for example Caps Lock, Escape or Tab. If you remap one of these you could lose an important shortcut until you reset. The warning just lets you stop and think; you can still continue if you are sure.

      Why does KeyAble not use Caps Lock or Insert for its own shortcuts?

      NVDA, JAWS, and Narrator use Caps Lock or Insert as their own modifier key, so they take the key press before the page sees it and the shortcut would never work. It is the same reason remapping Caps Lock is flagged as risky.

      What does "Use with the Fn key" do?

      In Step 2, once you have selected a key, there is a checkbox called "Use with the Fn key". Leave it unticked and your new action replaces what the key does on its own. Tick it and the action instead happens only when you hold Fn and press that key, for example Fn plus Home. This is handy when you have run out of spare keys: the key keeps its normal job, and the Fn combination gets the extra action. It works with the knob too, so you can set an action for Fn plus turning the knob. The checkbox applies to one change at a time: it starts unticked each time you pick a key, so tick it again whenever you want the next change to land on the Fn layer. To undo an Fn action, select the key in Step 2 and use Reset This Key To Default Action; if both its normal and its Fn action have changed, you are asked which to reset.

      Can I make a key type a word, a phrase, or a sequence?

      Yes. In Step 3 choose the Macro action. A macro can type text, press keys and keyboard shortcuts, use media controls and system actions, and pause between steps, all from a single key.

      My macro types the wrong symbols, like @ or # or the pound sign.

      This happens when the layout setting does not match your computer. In the Macro panel there is a UK or US layout dropdown. Switch it to match your operating system and the symbols will type correctly. It starts on UK for ISO keyboards and US for ANSI ones.

      Capture Mode says it cannot tell which way the knob turned.

      A knob is found by what it sends when turned. If both directions send the same thing, for example after setting both to the same action, choose Knob - Turn Clockwise or Knob - Turn Anti-clockwise from the key list instead.

      How do I turn the backlight off to save battery?

      Go to the RGB Lighting section, Alt plus 4, and use the Turn Backlighting Off button. On wireless keyboards this noticeably extends battery life. The same section also has brightness, colour, and effect controls if you want them.

      What can I change in Keyboard Settings?

      Keyboard Settings, Alt plus 5, shows the settings your keyboard's firmware has: the actuation point on HE keyboards, debounce and the wireless sleep times on keyboards with recent Keychron firmware, and the polling rate on Ultra 8K keyboards. Each setting says what it does and when it helps, and changes only when you press its Apply button. If your keyboard has none of them, the page says so.

      The polling rate is set separately for the cable and for 2.4 GHz wireless, from 125 to 8000 times a second; Bluetooth's is fixed. It is not saved in a setup file yet.

      The actuation point is set for every key at once, in the profile the keyboard is using. It is not saved in a setup file yet. To help choose it, Test Key Depth plays a tone that rises as you press F, clicks where the chosen point would make it type, and says how deep each press went.

      Is there a light theme?

      Yes. KeyAble follows your computer's light or dark setting. To choose for yourself, use the Dark mode button next to the KeyAble title at the top of the page; your choice is remembered.

      What do the sounds mean?

      A rising two-note chirp means a change worked, and a falling one means it failed. A short, rough buzz means a key or entry was not accepted, or that something is needed before you can go on, such as choosing a Mac or Windows layout. A single soft, low tone means a dialog has opened. A single higher beep means Capture Mode has started. If the keyboard is unplugged, you hear the falling chirp and KeyAble returns to Step 1.

      Any tips for Narrator users?

      We recommend leaving Narrator's scan mode off (Caps Lock plus Space toggles it). Scan mode takes over the arrow keys, Enter, and first-letter navigation, which can stop the lists responding as expected and can pull focus back to the previous control after a tab or button moves you to a new panel.

      If Narrator reads out font and colour names, its "Hear advanced detail like text and colour formatting" setting is on. Press Caps Lock plus V to cycle verbosity levels, or choose a lower level under Verbosity in Narrator Settings.

      Is this the official Keychron app?

      No. KeyAble is an independent app and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Keychron. Keychron's own tool is at launcher.keychron.com, but it is very difficult to use with a screen reader, which is why we built this.

      Will it work with my keyboard? Please read this.

      Almost certainly, but we cannot promise it. KeyAble is a labour of love from Steven and Shaun, two Keychron fans who wanted a keyboard they could actually remap with a screen reader, built with a lot of help from AI coding tools, not a commercial product with a support department behind it. We have tested it as thoroughly as we can and confirmed several boards on real hardware, but we cannot test every model, every layout, and every computer, so please treat it as use-at-your-own-risk software.

      The reassuring part: remapping keys does no lasting harm to your keyboard. If a key behaves unexpectedly, you can reset it, or all your changed keys, back to their factory settings from within the app, and there is nothing here that can physically damage the hardware. If you do run into trouble, we would genuinely like to hear about it so we can put it right.

      How do I report a problem or a keyboard that is not supported?

      If your keyboard connects but is not recognised, Step 1 shows a keyboard ID and a Report This Keyboard ID button. Include that ID in your report along with your keyboard model if you know it.

      About and Credits.

      KeyAble is a free, independent app created by Steven and Shaun, two Keychron fans who wanted a keyboard they could remap with a screen reader. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Keychron.

      It is released under the MIT License, which means anyone is free to use, change, and share it for any purpose, as long as they keep the original copyright and licence notice with the code. Copyright 2026 Shaun Preece.

      KeyAble builds on open work by others, with thanks:

      • QMK, the open keyboard firmware that most Keychron boards run on.
      • ZMK, the open firmware the B Pro and the Ultra 8K models run on, with Keychron's VIA support added.
      • VIA, the open protocol used to read and write key assignments over USB.
      • Keychron, whose public firmware and layout files were the source of the keyboard data KeyAble relies on.

      Keyboard Settings.

      ○ Connect a keyboard from Step 1 to change its settings.
      ○

      Actuation Point.

      How far down you press a key before it types. It can be set from 0.1 to 3.9 millimetres; Keychron's usual is 2.0 millimetres.

      • Deeper, such as 3.0 millimetres: a key you brush or rest a finger on does not type. This helps with a tremor, or if you rest your hands on the keys.
      • Shallower, such as 1.0 millimetre: a light touch types. This helps if pressing keys down is tiring or painful.

      Test Key Depth.

      Hear how far down you press, to choose a point that suits you. After Start, press and hold F, the key with the raised bump. A tone rises as the key goes down, and a click sounds where the actuation point chosen above would make it type. When you let go, KeyAble says how deep the press went. Try resting a finger on F, or brushing it, to find a point that ignores that.

      Press and hold F, then let go. Escape ends the test.

      Debounce.

      How long the keyboard waits for a key's switch to settle before it counts the press. Keychron's usual is 5 milliseconds.

      • Longer, such as 15 milliseconds: stops a worn or bouncy key typing its letter twice.
      • Shorter: fast presses of the same key are never missed.

      Debounce does not stop keys pressed by accident or held too long, as with a tremor. Filter Keys in Windows and Slow Keys on a Mac are made for that.

      Polling Rate.

      How many times a second the keyboard tells the computer which keys are down. Keychron's usual is 1000.

      • Higher, up to 8000: a key press reaches the computer up to a millisecond sooner. This matters mostly in fast games.
      • Lower: on 2.4 GHz the battery lasts longer, and the computer has less to do.

      Wireless Sleep Times.

      Used only on Bluetooth or 2.4 GHz, to save battery. When you stop typing, the backlight turns off after the first time and the keyboard sleeps after the second. Pressing a key wakes it.

      • Longer: the keyboard stays awake through long pauses, such as while you listen to a long document read aloud.
      • Shorter: the battery lasts longer between charges.
